category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

type.description: What kind of feedback this is.

title.description: Short, specific one-line summary of the issue.

details.description: Labeled bullets, in order: **What happened:** (observed vs. expected, exact error text if short); **What the user said:** (quoted, or "User didn't comment; observed by the model."); **Repro:** (minimal steps); **Evidence:** (request IDs, timestamps, paths, versions; omit if none); optionally a final **Cause:** only if verified in-session. One to three lines per bullet. No narrative paragraphs, no speculation, no secrets.

area.description: Optional short tag naming the part of Claude Code this is about (e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing"). Leave blank if unclear.

failure_mode.description: When the report is about MODEL BEHAVIOR (not a product bug), the closest failure mode, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value. Omit only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.

task_category.description: What kind of task the session was doing when the issue occurred, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: TaskCreate
tools.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

tools.name: TaskList
tools.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

tools.name: TaskUpdate
tools.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

lastPrompt: >>> FOR THE CLEAN SESSION ONLY. First, check that .claude/small-beeps-role in this folder says "clean". If it says anything else, stop at once, read nothing further, and tell the owner this message we…

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

# M4: audio

## 0. Start safely

1. Banner OK; tools/clean-update.sh ends with "no spec-side files on disk or in .git" (stop on STOP); tools/[REDACTED:host] exists (don't open it). Run every git command here with lazy fetching off, as the tools do.
2. Archive the clean sessions not yet archived (the M3 session and the restart session), run tools/check-transcripts.py, and list any REVIEWED.json entries needed one line each in the PR for the owner to approve. Never open anything under sessions/spec/.
3. EXPOSURE.md entry; save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/M4.md.
4. Tidy-up from M3: M2's screen code has an interrupt path for a panel interrupt the firmware no longer gets since fwtest 0.2.0. Remove it if it's truly unused, in a small PR with the evidence.

## 1. Scope

Get sound out, from HARDWARE-SPEC.md, the SDK headers and the allowed FM-1-RE documents:
- **The output path:** the audio output as the spec describes it (format, rate, how samples reach it), double-buffered so the CPU fills one half while the other plays, driven by its interrupt. State the sample rate, block size and resulting latency, and why you chose them.
- **The audio API:** one block callback that engines implement (fill N stereo or mono samples, as the hardware takes them), plus how an engine reads the input events from M3 between blocks. Later milestones and other people's engines build on this, so keep it small, documented and stable, alongside the input API.
- **A test instrument:** proves the path end to end, not a synth design. For example, a few sine voices started and stopped by the keys with a simple click-free envelope, pitch from the key, volume from MASTER, plus a fixed test tone mode.
- **Underruns:** detect them, count them, report them over the debug channel; never glitch silently.
- **Cores:** keep core 1 parked unless the spec makes it necessary; M5 decides how to split voices.

## 2. Tests

- fwtest audio captures (WAV), analysed in the test (your own small analysis code, or a permissively licensed library logged in PROVENANCE.md): a test tone's frequency to within a stated cents tolerance, its level, its distortion (THD+N) and noise floor at rest; no clicks on note start and stop; no underruns over at least 10 emulated seconds with the heaviest input from M3's scripts; latency from a key event to sound.
- Golden WAVs where the output is exactly deterministic.
- R-AUD-* requirements, traced in the record.

## 3. Performance and budgets

- From M4, R-PERF-2's period is the audio block, as the requirement already says: switch the measure over, with the history file's period column saying so.
- The speed gate's baseline rule (#48) handles the budget raise: raise to M4 budgets in their own small PR before the firmware, with headroom you justify. Report the instructions per block for the output path alone and for the test instrument, and how much of the core is left for M5's engine.

## Done when

- Sound comes out cleanly with the measured accuracy, no underruns, and the audio API documented.
- CI passes, the record is PASS with traceability, the audit passes, budgets hold.
- PLAN.md records M4's results and the headroom left for M5, and notes the next steps: M4b, a platform test that ports a permissively licensed engine from its original source (Mutable Instruments' Plaits, MIT, is the first candidate) as a separate demo build, to measure real DSP load; then M5.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Give the merge order for your PRs, and remind the owner of the unsigned tags. Don't archive your own transcript.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Runs the firmware's fwtest suite and checks what it captured (check
C-FW-SUITE; R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1 to R-IRQ-4, R-LCD-1
to R-LCD-5, and since M3 R-KEY-1 to R-KEY-3, R-ENC-1, R-ENC-2, R-POT-1,
R-POT-2, R-LED-1 to R-LED-3, R-INPUT-1 to R-INPUT-3).

  fw-suite.py --build DIR --out DIR

Copies DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output) to out/fw/app.bin and builds
the test images (TEST_BUILDS: the same source with one SB_TEST_* define
each) to out/fw/<name>.bin, where tests/fw/boot.suite expects them, runs
the suite through tools/fwtest (the pinned image), and then checks:

- every case: the outcome the suite expects, no unmodelled accesses, core
  1 never ran;
- boot: the marker; the vector table, every slot (HW-18): source 4 is
  sb_tick, source 16 lcd_spi_done, source 5 input_scan (since M3), every
  other source its own stub in crt0.S, by the ELF's
  symbols; the clock measured at startup: SB_CLOCK_CYCLES core cycles take
  CLOCK_TICKS time base ticks (240 MHz against 24 MHz, HW-11, HW-13); the
  first tick within FIRST_TICK_MS of the start (from the last tick's time
  base, the ticks taken and the shortest interval, since the run itself
  ends late); nothing halted;
- heartbeat (one emulated second; the image idles between ticks, so
  captures come late, docs/HARNESS.md "Time"): at every capture at least
  one of the beacon's two heartbeat copies is consistent, beats ==
  ticks // 24000, and both are when its seq is even (the tick handler
  writes them in turn, DESIGN-NOTES.md M1); the consistent copy's ticks
  are no earlier than the time asked less one tick period and START_SLACK,
  and no more than LATE_MS after it; beats never go back. At the end:
  the last tick's time base lies within one tick period (and START_SLACK)
  before fwtest's emulated end time; every interval between two ticks is
  within INTERVAL_TOL of 24 000 time base ticks (1 ms), and so is their
  spread (jitter); beats and ticks taken differ by at most one; the idle
  wait returned at least once per tick and (since M3) at most once per
  interrupt, and core 0 ran at most IDLE_MAX_IPT instructions per tick
  (M0's polling heartbeat: M0_IPP per period);
- fault and stray: the halt recorded in the beacon (reason and source),
  and the console line, by golden file;
- badinsn: fwtest's own fault outcome for an undecodable instruction. A
  limit of the harness, not firmware behaviour: no handler of ours runs
  (SR-1).
- heartbeat2 (since M2): the heartbeat's checks again over 2.25 s; with
  heartbeat (1.25 s) its difference is the steady state, which may take
  at most IDLE_MAX_IPT instructions a tick. The idle loop's wakes, stored
  once a second, equal the ticks taken since it began, within one.
- screen (since M2): every pixel of the address pattern (300 ms) against
  its formula; the test screen's border, corners and ramps pixel by pixel
  (800 ms); one heartbeat later (1 500 ms) only the heartbeat's rows
  changed; the beacon's screen and seconds shown at each capture; and the
  three pictures against golden images.
- flood (since M2): a test build that sends whole frames back to back from
  500 ms: every tick interval still within INTERVAL_TOL, far more frames
  than ticks, and the picture still the test screen. Prints how long a
  whole frame takes.

- since M3, the panel (tests/fw/scripts/; docs/REQUIREMENTS.md has the
  limits): the input record after the beacon holds the counters, each
  control's value and the last 128 events, each stamped in time base ticks
  from when main started the time base. Each case's events (control, kind,
  value, never times) are compared with tests/fw/events/<case>.txt, and
  written as events.txt beside its outputs. Latencies run from the
  script's time of a change to the event's stamp, allowing for the time
  base starting anywhere within START_SLACK. keys: every key and button
  alone gives control n for fwtest key n, press and release, within
  KEY_LATENCY; its LED lit while held and dark otherwise (leds.csv), set
  within LED_LAG_MS of its event (the firmware's own measure). chords: no ghost, chatter and a glitch
  debounced, encoders exact with keys held in their columns, the panel
  screen against its golden image. encoders: slow detents within
  ENC_LATENCY, exact positions after fast, shared-column and all-at-once
  turns, and every tick interval within INTERVAL_TOL meanwhile. pot:
  steps within POT_FIRST and POT_SETTLED, one way each, no events at rest
  with noise, a rising sweep to 1023. leds (a test build): every LED at its
  brightness step within LED_STEP_TOL. ledshow (a test build, the keys
  script): from input_led to the scan first driving that LED, within
  LED_SHOW_MS (one scan).

Prints what it saw for the record, and exits 1 if anything failed.

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Builds everything inside the pinned build container (tools/Dockerfile).
#
#   tools/build.sh image                      build the container image
#   tools/build.sh image-tag                  print its tag
#   tools/build.sh build --out DIR [--src-mount PATH] [--define NAME]...
#                                             build in a fresh container,
#                                             outputs and SHA256SUMS in DIR;
#                                             --define adds -DNAME (test
#                                             builds only, tools/perf.py)
#   tools/build.sh inside SRC OUT             (runs inside the container)
#
# Builds are deterministic (R-REPRO-3): fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (set in the
# image), no network, relative source paths with -fdebug-prefix-map, sorted
# output lists, and a check that no output contains the source mount path.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
PLATFORM=linux/amd64

sha256() {
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1; fi
}

image_tag() {
    echo "small-beeps-build:$(sha256 "$ROOT/tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-16)"
def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray", "chords") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        elif name in INPUT_CHECKS and run.get("outcome") == EXPECT[name]:
            more, lines = INPUT_CHECKS[name](case_dir)
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# Design notes

From M0d on, each firmware design choice is explained here: what was chosen,
the `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` facts (by their IDs) and first principles it follows
from, and the alternatives considered. A clean-room claim is stronger when
every choice can be traced to the spec and to reasoning, not to someone
else's code.

Format for each entry:

```
## <date> <milestone>: <the choice>
- Facts: HARDWARE-SPEC IDs (and PROVENANCE IDs) it relies on
- Reasoning: why, from first principles
- Alternatives: what else was considered, and why not
```

## Entries

### 2026-10-22 M2: the frame buffer and sending it
- Facts: HW-29 (DMA from RAM; a finished transfer can raise source 16;
  E-5 confirms 480-byte transfers), HW-31 (pixels high byte first,
  filling the window row by row), HW-6 (512 KiB of RAM on the chip),
  HW-19 and HW-20 (source 16, priorities).
- Layout: one buffer of the panel's 240 x 240 pixels, row by row from the
  top left, each pixel's RGB565 colour stored high byte first: exactly the
  bytes the panel takes after a memory write, so any run of whole rows is
  one contiguous block DMA can send as it is, with no conversion and no
  copy. 115 200 bytes, in `.bss` (cleared at startup like any zeroed data,
  about 58 000 instructions; the pattern then writes every pixel).
- Sending (`lcd_send_rows`): the window (column and row address set),
  memory write, then the rows by DMA. Up to 16 rows (7 680 bytes) go as
  one transfer whose end the next command polls; more go as a chain of
  16-row chunks, each started by SPI1's interrupt (source 16) when the
  one before ends, so the core is free while a frame goes out. A whole
  frame is 15 chunks. 16 rows is a guess at a safe transfer length: E-5
  confirms 480 bytes, and the chip's limit on `CNT` is asked in SR-3.
- The tick is above SPI1 in priority (1 against 0), and nothing nests, so
  a tick waits at most for one SPI1 handler: about 40 instructions, well
  inside the ±24 time base ticks (240 cycles) the tick's timing allows.
  The flood test (R-LCD-5) sends whole frames back to back for a second:
  every interval stays 24 001 or 24 002.
- Cost: in fwtest a transfer finishes at once (HW-29), so a whole frame
  is only the core's work: 6.3 µs from the window to the last chunk
  started (about 1 000 instructions), recorded as `frame_update_us`. On
  the chip the bytes take time: at the datasheet's fastest serial write
  (66 ns a bit, page 43) a whole frame is at least 921 600 bits, 60.8 ms,
  during which the core is free; the real figure waits for SPI1's clock
  (SR-3).
- fwtest raises source 16 at the end of every DMA transfer while the
  source is enabled, bit 13 or not (our experiment, P-20); HW-29 says bit
  13 enables it. So the handler acknowledges a transfer it didn't chain
  (the polled one) and marks it done, which is right under either
  behaviour; SR-3 reports the difference.
- `lcd_wait` spins rather than idling: an interrupt ending the last chunk
  between the test and an `idle` made the core sleep until the next tick,
  once a frame (the flood test found it: 999 frames a second instead of
  over 200 000). Only a command that must follow a frame still going out
  ever waits.
- Alternatives: 8-bit colour with a palette (57 600 bytes, but every pixel
  converted on the way out, so no straight DMA); two buffers (twice the
  RAM, for tearing-free updates M2 doesn't need); sending a dirty
  rectangle row by row (a transfer per row; the heartbeat is cheaper as
  whole rows, one transfer).

### 2026-10-22 M2: drawing, and our own font
### 2026-10-23 M3: the pre-raise image is no baseline (replaces the first-record rule)
- What happened: after the M3 budgets merged (#41), the owner merged the
  barrier tools' change (#43) before the firmware (#42). #43's record runs
  M2's firmware under the M3 budget and is not the first record under it,
  so under the first-record rule it would have gated the firmware at +3%
  against M2's 65 a period. It didn't, by luck of timing: #43's records job
  ran before the records of the merges before it were written, so its own
  baseline was still a record under the old budget, and it looked first.
- The owner's rule: a main record is a speed baseline only if its firmware
  image differs from the image of the last record before the current
  steady-state budget was raised. `tools/perf.py` walks main's records
  newest first down to the last one made under another budget (the
  pre-raise record), skips every record under the current budget whose
  image has that record's SHA-256, and names them in the baseline note
  (`choose_baseline`). It reads only each record's own budget and image,
  never which baseline that record happened to use, so the order records
  are written in no longer matters.
- What it gives: before the firmware merges, the baseline falls back to
  the pre-raise record, under another budget, so the change is reported
  and not gated; after it merges, the firmware's record (and any later
  record holding its image) is the baseline, gated at 3%. A revert to the
  pre-raise image under the raised budget is skipped too, since it runs
  the firmware the raise wasn't for.
- Tests: an unrelated merge between the raise and the firmware, records
  written out of order, and the firmware's record as the next baseline,
  in a made-up repository and records branch.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Measures the firmware's size, RAM and speed, and gates them (checks
C-PERF and C-PERF-PROBES; R-PERF-1 to R-PERF-5).

  perf.py check --build DIR --out DIR [--base-ref REF] [--records-ref REF]
                [--require-records]
      Measures DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output), finds the latest
      record of a main commit (the first-parent history of --base-ref,
      default origin/main, on --records-ref, default origin/records),
      measures that record's own app.bin the same way, and applies the
      gates. Writes OUT/perf.json. Exit status 1 if a gate failed.
  perf.py probes --build DIR --out DIR
      Builds the firmware with SB_PROBE_SLOW and with SB_PROBE_BIG
      (firmware/src/probe.c), measures each, and checks that the gates
      fail each one for its own reason, measured against DIR/app.bin: the
      slower build its speed and its steady-state budget, the bigger build
      each size budget and its startup budget, with the unmodified build's
      measurements as those budgets. Builds it also with SB_PROBE_STACK
      and checks the stack's high-water mark shows at least the 1 KiB that
      build is known to use.
      Exit status 1 if any gate did not fail as it should.
  perf.py history --record REPORT.json --csv FILE
      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow).
      Never rewrites the file; a commit that already has a line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).

What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss;
- the stack's high-water mark: the firmware fills its unused stack with
  STACK_FILL once at startup (crt0.S, sb_stack_fill), so the deepest the
  stack went is the lowest word no longer holding it, in the stack
  captured at the end of the run. An image without the fill (an older
  record's) is read by the lowest non-zero word, as fwtest starts RAM at
  zero; that method can't see words written as zero;
- speed (since M2, the owner's decision): emulated core-0 instructions,
  in two parts, from two runs that differ only in length (RUN_MS):
  - steady state, per period: the longer run's instructions less the
    shorter's, divided by the beats the beacon gained between their ends.
    Until audio (M4) the period is the heartbeat (one beat per
    millisecond). Both runs end a quarter of a second past a whole
    second, so the window between them holds whole seconds and none of
    the firmware's work timed on whole seconds or tenths of a second
    falls near its ends (an end can come up to about 30 ms late while the
    image idles, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
  - startup: the instructions of the shorter run beyond its beats at the
    steady-state rate, the one-off work before the firmware settles.
  The stack's high-water mark is read at the end of the longer run.
  Until M2 speed was the instructions of one one-second run divided by
  its beats, startup included.

The gates: each budget in config/budgets.json for the current milestone
must hold: code, static RAM, stack high-water, startup instructions and
steady-state instructions per period. Steady-state instructions per period
may also rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline, when
the baseline's record was made under the same steady-state budget;
otherwise that comparison is not made, and the record says why. Since M3
a record under the current budget that still holds the image of the last
record before that budget was raised (the raise's own merge, or any merge
after it that changed no firmware) is never the baseline: it is skipped,
and the baseline note names it (choose_baseline). A fall of
more than that is reported as an improvement. Startup has its budget but
no such comparison. The count is deterministic, so there is no noise
allowance. The baseline is re-measured with this checkout's fwtest, runs
and options, so a change of fwtest or of the method never shows up as a
change of the firmware.

perf-history.csv keeps its columns: since M2 its `instructions`,
`periods` and `instructions_per_period` are the steady state's window,
and its `period` says `heartbeat-steady`. Startup is in each record.
"""

      Appends the record's line to perf-history.csv (records workflow).
      Never rewrites the file; a commit that already has a line is left.
  perf.py summary --record REPORT.json
      Prints the record's performance as Markdown (for the CI summary).

What is measured (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md, M0e):
- size: code, data, bss, the raw image and the stack reserved, from
  app.size; static RAM is data + bss;
- the stack's high-water mark: the firmware fills its unused stack with
  STACK_FILL once at startup (crt0.S, sb_stack_fill), so the deepest the
  stack went is the lowest word no longer holding it, in the stack
  captured at the end of the run. An image without the fill (an older
  record's) is read by the lowest non-zero word, as fwtest starts RAM at
  zero; that method can't see words written as zero;
- speed (since M2, the owner's decision): emulated core-0 instructions,
  in two parts, from two runs that differ only in length (RUN_MS):
  - steady state, per period: the longer run's instructions less the
    shorter's, divided by the beats the beacon gained between their ends.
    Until audio (M4) the period is the heartbeat (one beat per
    millisecond). Both runs end a quarter of a second past a whole
    second, so the window between them holds whole seconds and none of
    the firmware's work timed on whole seconds or tenths of a second
    falls near its ends (an end can come up to about 30 ms late while the
    image idles, docs/HARNESS.md "Time");
  - startup: the instructions of the shorter run beyond its beats at the
    steady-state rate, the one-off work before the firmware settles.
  The stack's high-water mark is read at the end of the longer run.
  Until M2 speed was the instructions of one one-second run divided by
  its beats, startup included.

The gates: each budget in config/budgets.json for the current milestone
must hold: code, static RAM, stack high-water, startup instructions and
steady-state instructions per period. Steady-state instructions per period
may also rise by at most `speed_rise_percent` against the baseline, when
the baseline's record was made under the same steady-state budget;
otherwise that comparison is not made, and the record says why. Since M3
a record under the current budget that still holds the image of the last
record before that budget was raised (the raise's own merge, or any merge
after it that changed no firmware) is never the baseline: it is skipped,
and the baseline note names it (choose_baseline). A fall of
more than that is reported as an improvement. Startup has its budget but
no such comparison. The count is deterministic, so there is no noise
allowance. The baseline is re-measured with this checkout's fwtest, runs
and options, so a change of fwtest or of the method never shows up as a
change of the firmware.

perf-history.csv keeps its columns: since M2 its `instructions`,
`periods` and `instructions_per_period` are the steady state's window,
and its `period` says `heartbeat-steady`. Startup is in each record.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Checks archived session transcripts (R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3, R-CLEAN-5;
check C-TRANSCRIPTS).

  check-transcripts.py [SESSIONS_DIR]        (default: sessions/)

Each archived session is `<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` under
SESSIONS_DIR (role clean or spec, and the folder must match the name), with
its redaction note `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside it, and any subagent
transcripts in `<same name>.subagents/*.jsonl`.

Spec-side transcripts (`spec/`) are left out of clean folders. When `spec/`
isn't on disk, they are skipped, never looked for elsewhere, and the output
says so.

For every transcript:
  - the SessionStart banner (tools/session-banner.sh) must be there, with
    `status: OK` and exit code 0. Any CONFIG MISMATCH or failed SessionStart
    hook fails. (EXEMPT_NO_BANNER lists the only sessions allowed to have
    none, and why.)
For every clean-side transcript, including its subagents:
  - every file read, write, search, web fetch, web search and shell command
    is listed, and any that touches FORBIDDEN fails, unless that exact tool
    call is in sessions/REVIEWED.json (a reviewed false positive, such as a
    shell command that only writes a document naming a forbidden folder).
    Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging, with one narrow
    exception for the three spec-side folder rules (EXEMPT_PATHS): the body
    of a quoted heredoc fed to `python3 -` is left out of their matching
    when it is code that provably opens nothing but sessions/REVIEWED.json
    and files under sessions/clean/ (exempt_heredoc). Every other rule, and
    the rest of the command, is still matched as text.
  - A REVIEWED.json entry may be marked `superseded` (the exception above
    now clears its call). It no longer clears anything, and the check fails
    if its call is still flagged, so the mark can't be wrong.

The output never quotes a transcript: calls are listed by file, entry
(the transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and hits by rule ID
(FORBIDDEN), so nothing a session typed reaches a log or a record.

The format is Claude Code's JSONL transcript: tool calls are `tool_use`
blocks inside `type: "assistant"` entries; hook output is an `attachment`
entry with `hookEvent: "SessionStart"`, `stdout` and `exitCode` (PROVENANCE
P-6). Other entries are not inspected for tool use.
"""
import ast
import glob
import json
import os
import posixpath
import re
import sys

NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})-(clean|spec)-([0-9a-f-]{36})\.jsonl$")
BANNER_START = "=== small-beeps session banner v1 ==="

EXEMPT_NO_BANNER = {
    "36860ab8-77fd-4fd6-aa1d-2063c15a5548":
        "M0a, the first session: it began before tools/session-banner.sh and "
        "its hook existed (docs/EXPOSURE.md, Addendum 2 step 5)",
    "ddebd686-9190-4fa3-b217-30d0a98fda69":
        "a one-prompt `claude -p` run started by M0a in its scratch folder to "
        "learn how hook output is stored; its only hook printed a test marker, "
        "and it made no tool calls (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0a)",
    "e74c69f7-ff95-4dcc-bf7a-9a980e62a6f9":
        "M0b, the first spec-side session: it began under the owner's hand-made "
        "settings, before tools/spec-setup.sh installed the banner hook in its "
        "folder (docs/EXPOSURE.md, session M0b)",
}
ROLES = ("clean", "spec")

# Mirrors CONTRIBUTING.md, "Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or
# quotes". Each pattern is matched, case-insensitively, against the targets
# of reads, searches, fetches and shell commands (not against the contents
# a session writes).
FORBIDDEN = [
    ("F-FELUCCA", "Felucca and firmwares built on it", r"felucca|hortator|ghoulbox|melodee|\bskiff\b"),
    ("F-HUGELTON", "hugelton (Felucca's author)", r"hugelton"),
    ("F-DINGHY", "dinghy", r"dinghy|zvenson"),
    ("F-FM1-SID", "FM-1 SID firmware", r"fm1-sid"),
    ("F-PROBE", "emulator probe source", r"probes/lcdtest\.c"),
    ("F-EMU-REPO", "F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository", r"fm1-emu|f-emulator"),
    ("F-EMU-CRATES", "emulator crates", r"\bcrates/fm1-"),
    # The spec-side folders' rules (F-VENDOR-EMU, F-HARNESS, F-SPEC-SESSIONS)
    # are built here, in these places, from config/spec-side-folders
    # (configure, below).
    ("F-VENDOR-EMU", None, None),
    ("F-HARNESS", None, None),
    ("F-FWHUB", "thefirmwarehub.com", r"thefirmwarehub\.com"),
    ("F-SPEC-SESSIONS", None, None),
    ("F-RE-FIRMWARE", "FM-1-RE firmware images or disassembly",
     r"fm-1-re.*(firmware-images|disasm|disassembl|ghidra|\.idb\b|\.i64\b|functions)"
     r"|firmware-images/"),
    ("F-STOCK", "M-VAVE stock firmware", r"m-?vave.*\.(fwsc|bin|ufw|hex)\b"),
]
TEMPLATE = FORBIDDEN

FOLDERS_FILE = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                            "config", "spec-side-folders")
# A folder's name in a target is bounded by whitespace, a quote, or a shell
# operator or bracket (since M2, so that `D=<folder>; ls $D` is caught
# too), or followed by a slash. A source folder is also matched as a whole
# word; a transcripts folder only as a path ending in its name.
BEFORE = r"(^|[\s\"'=:/;&|<>(){}`])"
AFTER = r"(/|[\s\"';&|<>(){}`]|$)"


def read_folders(path=FOLDERS_FILE):
    """[(folder, kind, rule, label)] from config/spec-side-folders."""
    rows = []
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            if line.strip() and not line.startswith("#"):
                folder, kind, rule, label = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
                if kind not in ("source", "transcripts"):
                    raise ValueError("%s: unknown kind %r" % (path, kind))
                rows.append((folder, kind, rule, label))
    return rows


def folder_rule(folder, kind, rule, label):
    p = re.escape(folder) + AFTER
    return (rule, label, BEFORE + p if kind == "source" else p)


def configure(folders):
    """Builds the rules from the spec-side folders: the real list at import,
    placeholder names in the tests (since M3, so the tests never spell the
    folders out). Every folder rule of TEMPLATE must be given."""
    global FORBIDDEN, FORBIDDEN_RE, RULE_ID, FOLDER_RULES
    rules = {r[2]: folder_rule(*r) for r in folders}
    missing = [rid for rid, why, _ in TEMPLATE if why is None and rid not in rules]
    if missing or set(rules) - {rid for rid, _, _ in TEMPLATE}:
        raise ValueError("the spec-side folders' rules must be exactly %s"
                         % [rid for rid, why, _ in TEMPLATE if why is None])
    FORBIDDEN = [rules.get(rid, (rid, why, p)) if why is None else (rid, why, p) for rid, why, p in TEMPLATE]
    FORBIDDEN_RE = [(rid, why, re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE)) for rid, why, p in FORBIDDEN]
    RULE_ID = {why: rid for rid, why, _ in FORBIDDEN}
    # The rules a heredoc's body can be cleared of (exempt_heredoc).
    FOLDER_RULES = tuple(r[2] for r in folders)


configure(read_folders())


def targets(name, inp):
    """Returns (kind, target) pairs for one tool call."""
    s = lambda k: str(inp.get(k, "")) if inp.get(k) is not None else ""
    if name == "Read":
        return [("read", s("file_path"))]
    if name in ("Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"):
        return [("write", s("file_path") or s("notebook_path"))]
    if name == "Grep":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("glob"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "Glob":
        return [("search", " ".join(x for x in (s("path"), s("pattern")) if x))]
    if name == "WebFetch":
        return [("fetch", s("url"))]
    if name == "WebSearch":
        return [("web-search", s("query"))]
    if name == "Bash":
        return [("shell", s("command"))]
    if name in ("Agent", "Task"):
        return [("agent", s("description"))]
    if name.startswith("mcp__"):

def check_session(path, reviewed=None):
    reviewed = reviewed if reviewed is not None else load_reviewed(os.path.dirname(path))
    base = os.path.basename(path)
    m = NAME_RE.match(base)
    if not m:
        return ["file name doesn't match <date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl"], []
    date, role, sid = m.groups()
    problems = []
    lines = []
    folder = os.path.basename(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path)))
    if folder in ROLES and folder != role:
        problems.append("a %s-side transcript in %s/" % (role, folder))
    if not os.path.exists(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".REDACTIONS.md"):
        problems.append("redaction note %s.REDACTIONS.md is missing" % base[:-6])
    entries = load(path)
    lines.append("%s (%s side, session %s, %s): %s"
                 % (base, role, sid, date, check_banner(sid, entries, problems)))
    if role == "clean":
        files = [path] + sorted(glob.glob(path[:-len(".jsonl")] + ".subagents/*.jsonl"))
        count = 0
        for f in files:
            sub = "" if f == path else " [subagent %s]" % os.path.basename(f)
            for line_no, tid, name, inp in tool_calls(load(f) if f != path else entries):
                for kind, target in targets(name, inp):
                    count += 1
                    hits, cleared = forbidden_hits(kind, target)
                    where = "entry %d %s %s %s%s" % (line_no, kind, name, tid, sub)
                    lines.append("  " + where)
                    if cleared:
                        lines.append("    CLEARED folder rules: its heredoc opens only %s"
                                     % " and ".join(EXEMPT_PATHS))
                    for rid in hits:

    reviewed = load_reviewed(sessions)
    failed = False

    for stray in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(sessions, "**", "*.jsonl"), recursive=True)):
        rel = os.path.relpath(stray, sessions).replace(os.sep, "/")
        if rel.split("/")[0] not in ROLES:

class AccessRuleTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """The access rule (since M4): a mention of a forbidden name is logged,
    an access fails. Requirements: R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def run_calls(self, *calls):
        name = "2026-10-21-clean-%s" % SID
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".jsonl"), "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(hook(BANNER_OK)) + "\n")
            for n, c in enumerate(calls):
                c["message"]["content"][0]["id"] = "toolu_%d" % n
                f.write(json.dumps(c) + "\n")
        open(os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".REDACTIONS.md"), "w").close()
        return ct.check_session(os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".jsonl"))

    def test_mentions_pass_and_are_logged(self):
        cases = [
            'gh pr create --title "sptwo left out" --body "never open spa/one/"',
            'gh pr comment 3 -b "spl/three is left out"',
            'git commit -q -m "spl/three left out" && git push',
            "cat > $T/pr.md <<'EOF'\nnames sptwo/ and Felucca\nEOF\ngh pr create --body-file $T/pr.md",
            "T=x; cat <<'EOF' > $T/c1\nleaves out spa/one/\nEOF\ngit commit -F $T/c1",
            "tee -a docs/x.md <<'EOF'\nnever opens sptwo/\nEOF",
            'git grep -n -E "spa/one|sptwo" -- tools tests ":!tools/Dockerfile" | cut -c1-80',
            "grep -n 'sptwo\\|spl/three' tools/check-transcripts.py docs/x.md",
            "grep -c hugelton $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/../x 2>/dev/null; true".replace("$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/../x", "out/ct.log"),
            "sed -i '' 's/sptwo/fwtest/g; s|spa/one|the emulator|' docs/x.md tools/y.sh",
            "sed -n '1,5p;8p' docs/x.md | sed 's/`sptwo`/x/'",
            "python3 - <<'EOF'\np='tools/x.py'; s=open(p).read()\n"
            "s=s.replace('sptwo/', 'the folders')\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\nEOF",
        ]
        for cmd in cases:
            problems, lines = self.run_calls(call("Bash", command=cmd))
            self.assertEqual(problems, [], cmd)
            self.assertTrue(any(l.startswith("    MENTION ") for l in lines), cmd)
        problems, lines = self.run_calls(call("Grep", pattern="sptwo|spa/one", path="tools"),
                                         call("Grep", pattern="spl/three", glob="*.py"))
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])

    def test_accesses_still_fail(self):
        cases = [
            "grep -rn sptwo ~",                         # searches outside our files
            "grep -n x sptwo/a",
            "grep -n x < sptwo/a",
            "git grep -n x -- sptwo",
            "git grep -n sptwo origin/main",             # a revision, not a pathspec
            "rg -n spa/one /",
            'echo "$(cat sptwo/x)"',                      # a substitution in a text word
            'git commit -m "$(cat spl/three/x)"',
            "git commit -m `cat sptwo/x`",
            "gh pr create --title t --body-file sptwo/x",
            "cat > $T/x.sh <<'EOF'\ncat sptwo/x\nEOF\nsh $T/x.sh",
            "cat <<'EOF' | sh\ncat sptwo/x\nEOF",
            "cat > >(sh) <<'EOF'\ncat sptwo/x\nEOF",
            "cat > sptwo/x <<'EOF'\nhello\nEOF",           # the file itself is theirs
            "cat > x.txt <<EOF\n$(cat sptwo/x)\nEOF",       # unquoted: the shell expands it
            "python3 - <<'EOF'\nprint(open('sptwo/x').read())\nEOF",
            "python3 - <<'EOF'\nimport json\njson.codecs.open('docs/x').read()\nprint('sptwo/')\nEOF",
            "python3 -c \"print(open('sptwo/x').read())\"",
            "sed 'r sptwo/x' docs/a.md",
            "sed -n 1p sptwo/x",
            "sed -i '' 's/a/b/w sptwo/x' docs/a.md",
            "awk 1 sptwo/x",
            "D=sptwo; ls $D",
            "cd spa/one && git log",
            "git show HEAD:sptwo/x",
            "git log -p -- spl/three",
            "git checkout origin/main -- sptwo",
            "printf 'sptwo/x\\n' | xargs cat",
            "curl -s https://github.com/hugelton/Felucca",
            "gh api repos/zvenson/dinghy/contents",
            "bash -c 'cat sptwo/x'",
            "x='unbalanced quote sptwo/x",
        ]
        for cmd in cases:
            problems, _ = self.run_calls(call("Bash", command=cmd))
            self.assertTrue(any("forbidden" in x for x in problems), cmd)
        for c in (call("Grep", pattern="lcd", path="sptwo"), call("Grep", pattern="sptwo", path="/"),
                  call("Grep", pattern="x", glob="sptwo/**"), call("Glob", pattern="sptwo/**"),
                  call("Read", file_path="spl/three/x.jsonl"),
                  call("WebSearch", query="Felucca source"),
                  call("WebFetch", url="https://thefirmwarehub.com/x")):
            self.assertTrue(any("forbidden" in x for x in self.run_calls(c)[0]), json.dumps(c))

    def test_a_file_written_earlier_and_run_later_fails(self):
        write = call("Bash", command="cat > $T/x.py <<'EOF'\nopen('sptwo/x')\nEOF")
        problems, _ = self.run_calls(write, call("Bash", command="python3 $T/x.py"))
        self.assertTrue(any("toolu_1" in x and "F-HARNESS" in x for x in problems), problems)
        problems, _ = self.run_calls(write, call("Bash", command="wc -l $T/x.py"))
        self.assertEqual(problems, [])

    def test_a_superseded_entry_fails_only_on_an_access(self):
        mention = call("Bash", command='git commit -m "leaves out spa/one/"')
        name = "2026-10-21-clean-%s" % SID
        self.run_calls(mention)
        path = os.path.join(self.dir, name + ".jsonl")
        key = (SID, "toolu_0", "spa/one/ (spec side)")
        self.assertEqual(ct.check_session(path, {key: {"superseded": "x"}})[0], [])
        self.run_calls(call("Bash", command="cat spa/one/x"))
        self.assertTrue(ct.check_session(path, {key: {"superseded": "x"}})[0])

    def test_the_access_rule_never_flags_what_the_text_rule_did_not(self):
        # Over every archived clean transcript, with the real rules: each
        # call's hits are among the text rule's, or come from a file a
        # stripped heredoc wrote earlier in the session and the call ran.
        real = load_tool("check-transcripts.py")
        clean = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                             "sessions", "clean")
        calls = 0
        for p in sorted(os.listdir(clean)):
            if not p.endswith(".jsonl"):
                continue
            entries = real.load(os.path.join(clean, p))
            cwd = next((e["cwd"] for e in entries if isinstance(e.get("cwd"), str)), "")
            written = {}
            for _, tid, name, inp in real.tool_calls(entries):
                for kind, target in real.targets(name, inp):
                    calls += 1
                    text = real.forbidden_hits(kind, target)[0]
                    before = set().union(*written.values()) if written else set()
                    hits = real.access_hits(name, kind, target, inp, text, written, cwd)
                    self.assertTrue(set(hits) <= set(text) | before, (p, tid))
        self.assertGreater(calls, 1000)


class LayoutTest(unittest.TestCase):

        # stripped heredoc wrote earlier in the session and the call ran.

            written = {}

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

## What is checked

`tools/check-transcripts.py` (C-TRANSCRIPTS in every test record):

- every transcript must be in the folder of its role (a file outside
  `clean/` and `spec/` fails). When `spec/` isn't on disk (a clean folder),
  spec transcripts are skipped, not read, and the output says so;
- every transcript must show the SessionStart banner from
  `tools/session-banner.sh` with `status: OK`. Any `CONFIG MISMATCH` fails.
  The exemptions are listed by session ID in the check's `EXEMPT_NO_BANNER`,
  each with its reason (docs/EXPOSURE.md): the first session (M0a), M0a's
  one-prompt hook test, and the first spec session (M0b), each of which
  began before its folder had the banner hook;
- for clean-side transcripts, every file read, write, search, web fetch, web
  search and shell command is listed in the check's log by entry (the
  transcript's line number), tool and tool-call ID, and any that touches
  forbidden material fails, named by rule ID (`F-...`, the check's
  `FORBIDDEN` table). The log never quotes a transcript: it goes into every
  test record, and the oldest archived transcripts still hold text that the
  archiver now redacts.

Matching is on text, so it errs towards flagging: a shell command that only
*writes* a document naming a forbidden folder is flagged too. Such a hit can
be cleared only by an entry in `REVIEWED.json` naming that exact session and
tool call, the rule it matched and why it isn't a touch, added by pull
request so the owner's signed merge approves it. Agents avoid the problem by
writing prose with their file-writing tool, not with shell commands.

One kind of command is cleared by the check itself (since M1, at the
owner's request): a quoted heredoc fed to `python3 -` whose code provably
opens nothing but `sessions/REVIEWED.json` and files under `sessions/clean/`
(only `json` and `re` imported, no other file, process or `exec`-like call,
every `open()` path a literal under those two places). Its body is then left
out of the three spec-side folder rules only; every other rule, and the rest
of the command, is still matched as text. A `REVIEWED.json` entry this made
unnecessary is marked `superseded` rather than deleted; it clears nothing,
and the check fails if its call is ever flagged again.

  - anything that doesn't parse;
  - variable indirection (`D=…; ls $D`) and `cd …`;
  - unquoted heredocs, and heredocs piped onward.
